title: Emotions Unleashed
excerpt: The world feels chaotic — but does chaos begin outside us, or within our own minds? A reflection on the seven sins, the war between heart and logic, and why emotions are meant to be freed, not caged.
content:
Where to start? I guess the only option is to write. You know why? Because the world feels chaotic, but I wonder—does chaos really begin outside us, or inside our own minds? Our brain, with millions of neuronal connections, allows us not only to think but also to feel — making us humans.

Through Darwin’s evolutionary theory, human brains evolved greater complexities, giving rise to rules, expectations, emotions and inner conflicts. We are unique because of the emotions we feel, how we express them and what actions are made in those emotional state.

Our complex mind created the seven sins and we all know them by Pride, Envy, Wrath, Sloth, Greed, Gluttony and Lust. They are called sins as they pull the animal instincts out of the mind’s closet— instincts we often fear or deny.

So the pride and envy make us work for our status and success whereas gluttony, lust, and greed makes us have the uncontrollable urge to attain more food, sex and power. Wrath aka our anger, which we think spoils everything for us. So, Wrath simply responds to any threatening condition we encounter and can be triggered easily by other sins like fiery envy or our pride gets hurt. Lastly the Sloth, as it indicates slowness or laziness which is opposite to all other sins and lacks motivation. It gets activated, if there is no reason for us to do anything or simply our avoidance for unachievable goals. These sins brings out a different and scary individual that we can’t originally identify as ourselves.

Let’s get to know these sins a bit more!

So basically when humans encounter a situation, the mind works by understanding, interpreting and reaching an outcome after a lengthy process of pros and cons of that situation. As we think logically, simultaneously our emotions also come into action and then it’s a war between emotions and logics as we usually say “ a war between heart and mind”.

I have observed that emotions are complementary to our mind’s great logics. I wonder when Newton was sitting idle under a tree, but when he saw the apple falling, he thought of gravitational pull which was followed with his correct mathematics of gravity giving his EUREKA moment of life!! If emotions are always complementary, then question comes why to only see logic and always ignore or suppress emotions (mostly negative ones)?

Being a talkative person, I encountered answers for the above question too. The answer that topped is “ I am not emotional at all”. After listening this, I wonder that they might be using a lots of defence mechanism unconsciously like avoiding feelings, denying them, or acting in ways opposite to what they actually feel.

Second answer that comes into ears is that “ Emotions are for the weak, and I am not”. I am afraid of this one, because this actually gives a wrong illusion of weak and strong. People start questioning their own strength for dealing situations in their own individual’s life.

Then comes the answer is that “ If I let my emotions out, people will get to know my vulnerabilities.” People are always afraid of getting hurt,I know, but being vulnerable makes you more courageous and stronger. And some simply think that “emotions are waste of time.” This is the most funny one I guess! Because wether you agree or not, emotions (positive or negative) are the driving energy to move ahead in our lives.

I know it’s a bit technical, but I will try to make you understand in an easy way that how our acts are the consequences of our emotions. Positive emotions make us feel more happy and gratitude towards life and success. Our negative emotions drive us more fiercely towards our personal growth and goals (either good or bad). And often we tend to forget the importance of negative emotions.

As I stated the perception of people regarding their emotions, the most FAQ is that “How to stop feeling these emotions? Or How to be mechanical ? Or How to stop being weak or vulnerable ?? Or how do we stop getting ourselves hurt? Well dear readers, it may come as a surprise to you all, that the answer to all questions is “ NO , you CAN’T!” No human is born to become a robot by shutting is mind voluntarily, we don’t have this superpower.

Well, even if we try being mechanical, but yet somehow, our subconscious and unconscious mind does bring back those unresolved emotions relatively to our conscious mind, shouting at us to be seen.

All we have is an option to behave as human. Because suppression and bottling up emotions inside will do more harm and at some point, those emotions are gonna break free of your hold causing an inner conflict. Thus, it can give rise to mental struggles like low mood, anxiety, sleeping issues, or eating problems and many more.

The best way is to channelise these emotions and darkest sins in a healthy way. We need to learn what our emotions are trying to communicate with us and only if we resolve the reason, then only we can be free of those emotions.

Emotions are tricky even without the words, as most of the time these emotions manage to change our behaviour. And we often misinterpret the behaviour rather than noticing the feelings behind or the reason that caused it. Well, sometimes we relate with craziness of Harley Quinn or sometimes calm as Grand master Oogway and keep fluctuating between them!!

Historically, if we see, all the wars were driven by Pride, Greed or Lust. These days we fight but more internally than physical. Our daily events causes emotional stir too and affecting our interpersonal relations, profession, and our social life too. The first step to grow with your emotions is acknowledging . Just sit and breathe or shout or talk as per the convenience, but try focusing on why are you feeling this emotion? You reason with yourself and you will eventually reach an answer that will lead you to peace or mental calmness. Sooner acceptance and resolution will follow and the phase of this emotion will pass. Now, this ain’t a one day job! Don’t rush.

Just let the emotions flow, work slowly and you will be surprised with your own results. As we continue to live, the roller coaster of our emotions will keep us on exciting and thrilling journey, so just sit back and hold on tight and simply enjoy the ride. In the end, emotions are not to be caged— they are meant to be freed!

title: Redefining Love: A Beautiful Syndrome
excerpt: Medically, a syndrome is a cluster of symptoms — and so is love, a beautiful one. A look at the chemistry, history, and modern confusion of the emotion we chase the most.
content:
Well, we talk about love every day, yet we all try so hard to make sense of the love we are experiencing. Why syndrome? Because medically, I learned that syndrome is a cluster of symptoms. Similarly, love is a syndrome so beautiful that we always find ourselves flowing in its river of changing emotions- impossible to define, yet deeply felt.

“Love is all we have”, wrote Euripides. And as humans, love is perhaps what we yearn for the most. Everyone desires to be loved , to be acknowledged or to be liked. LOVE. It’s a four-letter word but expresses an array of emotions. That we all know, right!?

Love, from the Old English lufu, of Germanic origin; from an Indo-European root shared by Sanskrit lubhyati ‘desires’, Latin libet ‘it is pleasing’, libido ‘desire’. At its core, love is desire—raw, instinctive, human. Well, I had never quite thought it this way before! But when you are in love it’s simple, and it’s a strong feeling of attachment towards someone special (be it any gender) or object even.

We often notice that our mind goes blank. Butterflies take over the body and mind. This intense feeling or a chemical chain reaction which changes our physiology, psychology and behaviour feels similar to mild intoxication like altered perception, heightened emotions, and lowered inhibitions. Love brings out a whole new person in us which we want to explore more.

Our little brain holds its own “love circuit” which is filled with a cocktail of neurotransmitters and these small molecules stir the emotions associated with love. Love seems to be the collection of emotions like hope, happiness, sadness, excitement, jealousy, anger, comfort and what not! That’s why love has to be managed carefully.

The dopamine reward we receive when we are with our partners (again subjective!) and security via oxytocin builds the concept of love in our brain.

So, if you hear the word LOVE, what comes to your mind? That’s the question! The answer varies with every individual on this planet because of different personalities and one’s interpersonal relations and home environment moulds one’s mind and emotions. Most people have a tendency to relate it to God. But loving God is something different, something spiritual (Spirituality is whole another topic for another time).

For most people, love narrates the most meaningful chapters of life. For example, for some friendship is the main core, for others, riches are the emotions, while others explained love as pain, distance, devotion or letting go. And the unconditional love of family is evergreen.

I feel earlier times were simpler. According to drive theory, we all are derived to fulfil the biological needs and maintain balance in our minds and body. Sexual motivations were driven to have a mating partner and to fulfil procreation. In its earliest form, love was closely tied to survival. But as the world evolved, so did love.

What was once a simple biological drive became layered — filtered through screens, shaped by hashtags, and narrated in 30-second reels.

So, do we define it according to what world tells us or by the chemistry we experience with our partner?! Huh! Amazingly the upcoming mind-numbing concepts of bread crumbing, nanoship, situationship, orbiting, DTRs (define the relationship), cushioning, shrekking and so many others seems to have distorted the view point for love. Well, while our minds are busy learning these terminologies, we usually find ourselves ghosted!

But, it doesn’t matter how you define it. It’s what you feel, how you choose to express it and how safe you feel being seen. For love, actions speaks much more louder than words. So rather than asking questions of doubt like how much to invest emotionally? Or is the person right for me? Or anticipating things that have not happened yet? Just try to follow your instinct and let your actions do the work of defining your love for the person over time (not ignoring the red flags per se).

Because in the end, love is not about the definitions we invent or the words we chase. It’s about the moments that make us feel alive — the warmth in the ordinary, the madness in the meaningful, and the choice to stay when everything else changes.

So I say Be a little Foolish, be Hopeful Romantics and create your own memorable chapters. But also be gentle with your own limits and keep loving yourself no matter what.

title: When the Healer Needs Healing
excerpt: We swear by “do no harm,” yet forget to apply it to ourselves. On burnout, stigma, and the quiet mental-health struggles of the doctors who care for everyone else.
content:
OK! So we all know that health is not just the physical being—it’s also about how we are doing socially and mentally. Mess with the balance, and we might end up with some health problems. With our awareness of the mortality, we do keep our focus on physical health. But it seems that we often neglect our social and mental well being. Becoming a health professional isn’t a walk in the park, but our perseverance, hard work, and dedication keeps us pushing forward. Since Hippocrates’ days, doctors have come a long way, modernising the medical practice. We swear by the “Do no harm” oath, but somehow, we forget to apply it to ourselves.

Historically, society labelled healing as witchcraft and mind-healers as alienists. Over time, society has acknowledged physicians and physical diseases, yet a stigma for mental health persists. Despite psychiatry being part of the medical curriculum, it remains underrated among medicos. Psychiatry comes from Greek: psyche (mind/soul) and iatreia (healing). It addresses abnormal beliefs, emotions, and behaviour as mental illness. Our brain believes what we see, leading to supernatural views of unseen dysfunction. Ongoing brain research is providing evidence for mental illnesses. Also post-COVID period has significantly erupted with increased mental health awareness.

And yet, mental health among medicos remains in the shadows. There can be two major reasons for this. First, trying to acknowledge mental health can be overwhelming. Second is the lack of time due to overburdening workloads. A recent survey by Indian Medical Association (IMA) reported that over 80% of doctors are stressed out in their profession. It is quite ironic how we advise our patients to lower stress levels while we struggle ourselves.

The Yerkes-Dodson law states that too little or too much stress/ arousal results in poorer performance. Excessive stress can lead to burnout, anxiety, depression, decreased cognitive performances, substance abuse, sleep disorders, and many more. In striving to be tireless caregivers, we often forget that we are humans too. But the hardest part is to admit and accept the mental health challenges while wearing a heavy crown of healer. Our profession is noble and comes with lots of sacrifices to hold the legacy.

According to recent survey by NMC, 28% UG students and 15% PG medical students have mental health disorders including depression and anxiety. Nearly 16% of the UG students and 31% PG students reported suicidal thoughts. A study of 2019 shows 66.67% of resident doctors face personal burnout, 57.14% face work burnout and 16% report client- related burnout. Burnout is not mental illness per se but it is becoming a serious problem for the doctors.

Anxiety disorders can readily arise in students who are constantly managing emergencies, surgeries, critical care, or working in high-pressure departments and toxic work environments; at the same time unhealthy coping, including substance use can worsen the outcomes. There are other mental health issues like OCDs, panic disorders , parasomnias, atypical depression, phobic disorders, personality disorders etc which are still under the carpet.

Under the Dunning-Kruger effect for overestimating our coping skills, we all start thinking that we can handle everything but sooner or later, we dig a mental pit for ourselves. It is filled with our defensive behaviour, overthinking, apprehension about future, self doubt and comparison with others. These pits keep getting overloaded with other stress like work, studies, interpersonal conflicts etc. If these are not unloaded, they overflow with irritability, poor performance, sleep deprivation, questioning our own chosen careers, isolation from peers and family, loneliness, depersonalisation or derealisation, and many more.

But, Do we acknowledge all these things happening with us? No, the only thing we didn’t learn is the acceptance to our thoughts and mental conflicts which causes denial at so many levels pulling us deeper into our mental cages. Over time, these cages become our comfort zones, making it even harder to seek help. So, we avoid going to the psychiatry department when needed. I get it. I mean there is hesitance ofcourse, thoughts about social and peer judgement, getting labelled with disorders and biggest fear to see our own inner demons.

As doctors, we understand it anatomically, we must try to understand its functioning as well. Functioning of brain depends on the circuitries and neurotransmitter levels whose imbalance relates with onset of mental disorders. The genetics, biological factors (physical health, disability, sex, sleep), social factors (peers, house environment, work environment), and psychological factors (coping skills, social skills, self esteem, trauma) can shape the development of mental disorders. So, for our body to function properly, we all need to keep our brains healthy too.

The first step towards good mental health is to acknowledge our own state of mind either positive or negative. We need to let go the cape of shame in order to make our second move. Third, accepting and trusting that these disorders are treated professionally. Lastly, to give yourself a chance to heal holistically too. Though treatment takes time, but eventually unloading all the chaos and untangling the knots can be the real healing. I hope that the least we all medicos could do is try.

title: Rowing Through Expectations
excerpt: Imagine a boat so laden with farewell gifts you can barely row. On the weight of others’ expectations, the emotions tangled beneath them, and learning which gifts truly belong on your boat.
content:
OK, imagine this! You are on a boat, ready to venture into the sea. But the farewell gifts are so many that you find it difficult to row the boat. You try as much as you can but are unable to put any weight down as each gift carries a sentiment. Everyone expects you to take all the gifts for your journey. At some point, the journey isn’t about rowing harder—it’s about deciding which gifts truly belong on your boat.

Expectations are innate to human behaviour. The expectations and emotions that follow after the birth of a child are enormous. The expectations of parents start from the child’s future, gender roles, appearance, etc., and the list seems endless. So we grow up fulfilling the expectations of people around us. And when our prefrontal cortex develops, questions start arising retrospectively.

While growing up, we admire our parents, teachers who do so much for us. But sometimes, the phrases we hear are like, “we have raised you, we gave you everything, we are providing for you, we teach you so make us proud, and many more like this”. These words have both love and weight. A love so unconditional that it wants to guide us to the path of excellence. And a weight disguised as pride and happiness that some of us can’t provide. The expectations of two different paths for our lives don’t align. This is when their motivation becomes wrapped in our own guilt. How long do you think it can really sustain us!?

I feel some expectations exist at the same time but only one can be fulfilled by us. And the clashing expectations cause conflicts. For example, our personal expectations always clash with the societal expectations (which by the way mostly get preferred every time). And I am sure you must be thinking about your own mismatched expectations right now. These expectations shape us and our own views about self and another self that society is expecting us to be.

We all have personal expectations, social expectations, life expectations, career expectations, expectations in relationships, and many more that our tiny little brain can make. Don’t you feel drowning in this ocean of expectations? Sometimes, when we carry others’ expectations, their encouragement lifts us (Pygmalion effect), and low expectations could shrink us (Golem effect). Therefore, at times, we need to learn that expectations needs boundaries—not distance but clarity to row your boat more freely.

Have you ever observed how this unfolds in our lives? Take, for instance, how we study diligently when our parents and teachers commend us. Conversely, we tend to get into more mischief when people expect nothing from us. Often, we find ourselves in situations where we have neither others’ expectations to meet nor our own to chase. This results in an internal struggle between the reality and what we expected, leading to emotional turmoil. Thus, conflicts in expectations can also lead to conflicts in our emotions.

You must be thinking, why did I connect expectations with emotions? You know how the common saying goes, “No expectations, no disappointments”! What I feel is quite the opposite. Because when expectations don’t meet our own reality, the emotional turmoil starts. The escalated emotions might make us stray from our goals and ultimately away from fulfilling our own expectations. Or it could become a sign to learn from these emotions for the desired change to fulfil the expectation in our heads. Because sometimes it’s harder to deal with remorse or regret of not even trying either way.

We all expect our lives to be lived in a certain way. Little expectations make our lives go. We talk a lot about healthy and unhealthy lifestyles; likewise, there are healthy and unhealthy expectations. These healthy expectations guide us, motivate us, and are flexible enough to move forward toward our goals. While unhealthy ones might cage us in our own rigidity and fear of not matching the outcome as expected. Our boat tries to stay balanced between the tides of both expectations.

It’s very important for us to have expectations because without them, we won’t be having goals or a path to our lives. But whatever decision we make, we should be able to carry the weight of expectations, which will be coming alongside the consequences. If the weight becomes immovable like a mountain, we need to ask questions like, “Is this expectation mine or borrowed?”, “Does it expand me or shrink me?”, “What emotions sit underneath it—fear, pride, love, shame?”. Answering your own questions will surely help to lift off some of the weight.

We always have the power to become stronger. These tiny little machines in our heads, our minds, can absorb lessons from past experiences and use them to make wiser predictions for the future. By sharing our burdens with the people we are close to, we lighten the weight on our hearts. When our brain is free of fog, our thoughts flow with more clarity, and we can see the path ahead with sharper focus. The clarity will bring the courage to become better as life unfolds.

Whether it’s the journey of weight loss at the gym, mastering chess, completing an assignment, or any personal or social plans like meeting a friend or practicing dancing, these small expectations in our goals keep us motivated. We feel happier when our expectations align with the outcomes, but we emerge even stronger when they don’t. This is because we strive harder to meet our expectations, leading to our growth.

Therefore, I believe expectations shouldn’t be suppressed but rather guided appropriately. They should align with your reality to make them achievable. Sometimes, to accomplish something, we must be prepared to stand up for our happiness and goals. We often say we live only once. So, dear readers, give your best effort to achieve what you expect from life and take a break when needed. You don’t have to throw every gift away. Just don’t sink trying to carry them all.

title: The Cage We Built: Stigma, Society, and the Self
excerpt: Society was built for belonging and protection — so why does it so often cage us in stigma and silence? On stress, judgment, and why the real fight may be within ourselves.
content:
Our beloved word ‘society’ comes from French word “société”, rooted in the Latin “societas”, meaning “a friendly association with others”. If we look into history, we find that in 19th century, anthropologists divided human social evolution into three stages namely savagery (hunting), barbarism (gathering), and civilisation (family & urban life). So basically, society was built to have protection, belonging, and the basic means of survival.

But in modern times, society has evolved into a hub of individualisation (basic unit of an individual), specialisation or differentiation (specialised tasks in social system) and abstraction (being guided by experts and general rules). Therefore, the individuals are left alone to shield themselves from the societal rays of norms and stigma.

Interestingly, my focus here, is on “stigma”. The word comes from the Latin word stigmat-, meaning a “mark” or “brand”. In earlier centuries, the word was used for scar left by hot iron, which was said to have been “stigmatized”. The scar has become figurative in modern times, so stigma also refers to a “set of negative and often unfair beliefs that a society or group of people have about something”.

From the division of continents to transformation into different races, there are over 3814 distinct cultures that evolved and are reported by anthropologists. I wonder how many rules must be there to bind an individual to remain a part of society?! I guess a lot! Because we are taught that if we don’t do certain things in a certain way, people will not be accepting us or we will remain an outcast or we might bring shame upon the family and many more negative comments.

And I know we have been working hard according to what our culture, society demands in order to avoid the humiliation or just to stay accepted by our society. Seems like the rules are damn tight! Have you ever wondered what might happen if we derail from these rules? I agree it creates a huge conflict in our mind. A catastrophe in our own brain! Right?!

The word “stress” which is now commonly used, impacts our minds on whole another level. As per WHO, Stress is defined as a state of worry or mental tension caused by a difficult situation. And the difficult situation is known as a stressor. So stressors are different for every individual, it varies from getting a scolding to losing a big amount of money. These stressors sink deeper in our brain with heavy weights waiting to be lifted.

In today’s world, constantly juggling our past, future and our present has short-circuited our little Time Machine — the brain. The fuel (neurotransmitters) required for our brain to work becomes uneven and therefore causes poor mental health. These days people are chasing money, physical health, jobs, relations which makes me wonder that are we becoming more like zombies with no brain or are we avoiding situations because it’s too much to deal with? Well, our brain works in mysterious ways as it keeps on reminding us what needs to be dealt with. So the issues that are bothering us will keep resurfacing until we start acknowledging them.

We’re surrounded by people, yet the fear of judgment or ridicule silences us. We are habitual of swallowing our problems instead of speaking them. I believe that our struggles change with changes in the different era. From the Stone Age era to the Iron Age era and leading to the atomic era, now finally entered into Internet age. So as the name suggests, we can all think of lots of struggles back then for the people existed at that time. It must have been hard for them too but they found solutions which led us to all the technologies our brains could have imagined back then. But we forgot that modern era will give us our own puzzles to solve.

We all know that “Change is the only constant” and yet we often ask ourselves only one word… how?!

Situations arise every day in our lives, some handle them with grace, while for others, they feel like mountains too heavy to move. But that doesn’t mean they are weak, right? Because moving a mountain needs more manpower. Still the fight against the societal expectations continues. Not believable! Right? Because we are so open regarding mental health issues and talking about such issues on Internet platforms. But Are we really unwrapping the issues on ground level? Why is it difficult to identify problems?

When we encounter someone struggling, their words and hints are often masked. I get it, that not everyone can know about the signs and symptoms of a mental disorder but we can always tell the vibes! What we usually do is leave the person alone either due to his own unwillingness to show the vulnerability or our lack of patience to sit a bit longer with them. The common phrases we use include- “ You did that before, you can do it now.”, “ You are not alone, everyone else is also in the same boat”, “ it’s been long time, you should get over this soon”, “ You are getting weak if you keep doing this”, “ we all have been through the same thing, give time and it will heal” and many more like this. But we certainly don’t wait, and we expect that the person in front of us to have the same mental strength we have. Sometimes, all we need is support. Maybe just being there, trying to put ourselves in their shoes and showing empathy to them may bring a ray of light in their dark world.

In this age of “avoidance” and “moving on”, people often carry their emotional baggage while pretending to let go— until exhaustion takes over. What society gives them is very little time to assess which in turn makes them stumble and fall. We, as a society, don’t seem to be helpful enough to lift up the fallen ones. Society is the sole creator of stigma and should become the Breaker now. Mental health is of utmost importance now which we usually take for granted. Maybe the real fight isn’t against the society— it’s within ourselves. We need to learn how to unmask the reality of issues and reach their solution. The major issue still remains with acknowledging one’s poor mental health and when to demand help. To achieve good mental health, I believe we need to create healthy environment (society) for our minds to flourish and unlock the happiness within. For all my readers, Keep up the hard work of maintaining the sanity with this racing world.
